newsitem.title: UK: UK building firms lead business confidence higher.
newsitem.headline: UK building firms lead business confidence higher.

text.p: A marked turnaround in Britain's construction sector is a key factor in increased business confidence for the first quarter of 1997, according to a survey by Dun and Bradstreet.

The poll, which covered more than 1,600 company heads across all regions and sectors of British business, showed more than 70 percent of building firms expect a rise in sales in the first three months of 1997 and over 20 percent expect greater profits.
"This is first time for some years that there has been such a marked upturn in confidence in the construction sector," said Philip Mellor, D&B's senior analyst.
"Land and property prices are beginning to rise once again and this is closely related to general optimism within the construction sector."
D&B said the survey showed that 63.5 percent of all businesses now expect to take on more staff, compared with only 60.5 percent in the last quarter of 1996.
But the survey added that the forthcoming British election, which must be held by May 22, was expected to spark a slight slackening of business confidence in the short term.
Confidence in the export sector declined, D&B said, suffering from recent strength in the pound. But this was positive for inflation -- particularly imported inflation -- which should remain low.
